script: Most people get this backwards. They start investing before they have an emergency fund. Here's the problem: without 3 to 6 months of expenses saved, one job loss forces you to sell your investments at the worst possible time. Build your emergency fund first. Then invest with a clear head.

hook: SIP or lumpsum? Here's the real answer.
script: SIP or lumpsum? Here's the real answer. If you already have the money, research shows lumpsum often wins because markets rise more often than they fall. But if you're investing from salary, SIP wins because it removes the guesswork entirely. The best plan is the one you'll actually stick to.

hook: A 1 percent fee is costing you lakhs.
script: A 1 percent fee is costing you lakhs. Over 25 years, a 1 percent higher expense ratio can mean lakhs of rupees less in your final corpus. Always check the Total Expense Ratio before choosing a fund. It's one of the few things in investing you can control completely.

hook: Your credit score has nothing to do with your income.
script: Your credit score has nothing to do with your income. It's based on repayment history, credit utilization, and credit age. A high earner who misses payments can score worse than someone earning half as much who pays on time. Pay every bill on time. That's 90 percent of the game.

hook: No-cost EMI is rarely actually no-cost.
script: No-cost EMI is rarely actually no-cost. The interest is frequently built into a higher product price upfront. Before taking the offer, check the straight cash price elsewhere. That 2-minute check can save you real money.

hook: You're probably paying a hidden commission.
script: You're probably paying a hidden commission. Regular mutual fund plans include a distributor commission baked into the expense ratio. Direct plans skip it, saving you 0.5 to 1 percent a year. Over 20 years, that difference compounds into a meaningfully larger corpus.

hook: Your salary hike is quietly disappearing.
script: Your salary hike is quietly disappearing. Lifestyle inflation rarely feels like overspending in the moment, just small upgrades. Try this instead. Increase your SIP by the same percentage as your raise, before your lifestyle absorbs the extra income.

hook: Buy insurance before you buy investments.
script: Buy insurance before you buy investments. A single uninsured medical emergency can undo years of disciplined saving. Make sure health and term cover are in place first. Then build your investment portfolio on a protected foundation.

hook: Even professionals can't time the market.
script: Even professionals can't time the market. Study after study shows fund managers consistently fail to call the exact top or bottom. A disciplined SIP across market cycles tends to beat most attempts at perfect timing. Stop waiting for the perfect entry point.

hook: Stop checking your portfolio every day.
script: Stop checking your portfolio every day. Daily tracking fuels anxiety and impulsive decisions. Track your net worth once a quarter instead. Assets minus liabilities. That single number shows real progress without the noise.

hook: Vague goals rarely survive a tempting purchase.
script: Vague goals rarely survive a tempting purchase. Set your financial goals in writing with a rupee amount and a year attached. Twenty lakh for a house down payment by 2031, for example. A specific goal is much harder to abandon than a vague wish.

Debt funds are not risk-free. They carry interest rate risk and credit risk. A debt fund label doesn't mean guaranteed returns like a fixed deposit. Always check the average maturity and credit quality before assuming it behaves like cash.
